question.problem: Given that $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-3\cdot {2}^{x}$, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Applying the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-3\cdot {2}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5))-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\cdot {2}^{x}) \\  & =0-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({2}^{x}) \\  & =-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\cdot {2}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\cdot {2}^{x})|}_{x=1} \\  & =-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\cdot {2}^{1} \\  & =-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\cdot 2 \\  & =-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(2).\end{aligned}
$$
